summary.text:
For whether Yeti could move into fly fishing, the results offer only a partial cultural analysis of the fly fishing territory. The place exemplars share no filtered cultural signal at a consistent level, and no relative position or robustness could be established against a comparison set. A brand-conditioned query does return a supported set of associated entities, but the evidence cannot say how a move would be positioned relative to other territories or whether it is viable.
Fly Fishing: Fly fishing is represented by a small place panel of exemplars that Qloo links to the concept, so this read rests on those place examples rather than a full comparison set. Filtered shared cultural signals across the exemplars fall in no band and none are consistently shared, so the place examples show little common cultural signal in this analysis. The brand-conditioned query returned supported entities led by names such as Rainbow Trout Ranch and Blackberry Farm, an association within the returned list only, with evidence quality at medium and the list truncated.

followUpOptions: Add reference territories with a larger comparison set so a relative position and robustness can be assessed for fly fishing.
Pull additional fly fishing exemplars beyond the current place panel to broaden the shared-signal read.
Run brand-conditioned queries on adjacent outdoor activity territories to create a comparison set for the fly fishing result.
Investigate other entity types linked to fly fishing, such as brands or products, to see whether the association holds beyond places.
